# What is Nix?

## Nix is just another Programming language

Just like Java or Python or Bash.

```nix
let
  fizzbuzz = n:
    if n % 15 == 0 then "FizzBuzz"
    else if n % 3 == 0 then "Fizz"
    else if n % 5 == 0 then "Buzz"
    else builtins.toString n;
in
  builtins.genList (i: fizzbuzz (i + 1)) 10
```

It's not an "operating system" or "package manager." But it can do both of those things. More on that later.

## Nix functions can return *anything*



But unlike the languages you're used to, Nix doesn't just return 

```nix
{ pkgs, ... }:
pkgs.writeTextFile {
  name = "hello.txt";
  text = "Hello, world!\n";
}
```

It's not printing to the terminal. It's *return*ing a binary file!

```
╭─wolf at wolf-laptop in /tmp/tmp.RmsgK6BtQ0
╰─○ cat result                   
─────┬───────────
     │ File: result
─────┼───────────
   1 │ Hello, world!
─────┴───────────
```

## And you can compose *anything*

::: {.code-40}
```nix
let
inner = pkgs.writeTextFile {
  name = "inner.txt";
  text = "I am the inner derivation.";
};
in
pkgs.writeTextFile {
  name = "outer.txt";
  text = ''
	I am the outer derivation.
	The inner derivation lives at: ${inner}
	Inner contents:
	${builtins.readFile inner}
  '';
};
```
```nix
╭─wolf at wolf-laptop in /tmp/tmp.RmsgK6BtQ0
╰─○ cat result 
─────┬───────────
     │ File: result
─────┼───────────
   1 │ I am the outer derivation.
   2 │ The inner derivation lives at: /nix/store/cn5lv3xaky5mp8zqijfnn9sgr18yvy22-inner.txt
   3 │ Inner contents:
   4 │ I am the inner derivation.
─────┴────────────
```
:::

## Nix is an *Operating System*

Inputs

- Nixpkgs (more on this later)
- Linux kernel Source
- Stdenv (includes bash, coreutils, etc)
- A bunch of config files ~/.config/..., /etc/...
- A touch of magic 

## Nix is an *Operating System*

Outputs:

- The **Exact** state of my computer

```nix
{
  description = "An ENTIRE system configuration";

  inputs = {
    nixpkgs.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable";
  };

  outputs = {
    self,
    nixpkgs,
    ...
  } @ inputs: {
    nixosConfigurations.my-nixos = nixpkgs.lib.nixosSystem {
      system = "x86_64-linux";
      modules = [
        {
          users.users.wolf = {
            description = "wolf";
            openssh.authorizedKeys.keys = [
              "ssh-ed25519 %3Csome-public-key%3E wolf@wolf-pc"
            ];
            packages = with pkgs; [firefox];
          };
          services.openssh = {
            enable = true;
            settings = {
              PermitRootLogin = "no";
              PasswordAuthentication = false;
            };
            openFirewall = true;
          };
        }
      ];
    };
  };
}
```

## Nix is *everything*

::: {.code-40}
```nix
{
  description = "minimal nixvim config";

  inputs = {
    nixpkgs.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable";
    nixvim.url  = "github:nix-community/nixvim";
  };

  outputs = { nixpkgs, nixvim, ... }:
    let
      system = "x86_64-linux";
      pkgs = import nixpkgs { inherit system; };
    in {
      packages.${system}.default =
        nixvim.legacyPackages.${system}.makeNixvim {
          plugins = {
            telescope.enable = true;
            treesitter.enable = true;
            lualine.enable = true;
          };

          opts = {
            number = true;
            relativenumber = true;
            expandtab = true;
            shiftwidth = 2;
            tabstop = 2;
          };

          keymaps = [
            {
              key = "<leader>ff";
              action = "<cmd>Telescope find_files<cr>";
            }
          ];
        };
    };
}
```

# With nix, you can...

## Have a consistent developer environments

With nix, you can guarantee that everyone on your team has the exact same tools. You aren't guaranteeing they have the same versions. You are guaranteeing they have the *EXACT* same tools.

::: {.code-40}
```nix
{
  description = "Wolf's Personal Website";

  inputs = {
    nixpkgs.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable";
    flake-utils.url = "github:numtide/flake-utils";
    myResume = {
      url = "github:404wolf/resume-v2";
      inputs.nixpkgs.follows = "nixpkgs";
    };
  };

  outputs =
    {
      self,
      nixpkgs,
      flake-utils,
      ...
    }@inputs:
    flake-utils.lib.eachDefaultSystem (
      system:
      let
        pkgs = import nixpkgs { inherit system; };
      in
      {
        packages.default = pkgs.callPackage ./nix/build.nix { inherit (self.inputs) myResume; };
        devShells.default = pkgs.mkShell {
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID = "02e54289e54c9bca7d99203f8df8c230";
          PUPPETEER_SKIP_CHROMIUM_DOWNLOAD = "true";
          PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH = "${pkgs.chromium}/bin/chromium";
          packages = with pkgs; [
            nodejs
            pnpm
            typescript
            nil
            nixd
            nixfmt-rfc-style
            (pkgs.writeShellScriptBin "mmdc" ''
              exec ${pkgs.mermaid-cli}/bin/mmdc -p puppeteer-config.json "$@"
            '')
            chromium
          ];
        };
      }
    );
}
```
:::

## Your stuff *never* breaks

You can come back to your old janky project 40 years later.

- Your computer's Python installation is 50.99.99
- Javascript doesn't exist anymore
- CWRUnix is now a 501c religion (not a cult!)
- Case built another stupid 300M building
- Kaler makes 1,000,000\*1.1^40=\$\$\$45M :)

And run `nix build`

And it "just works." I know it sounds too good to be true. I know.

## Let's dive a bit deeper

### Nix is *Different*

Okay, so nix is a little different from the languages you're used to.

### Nix is a *lazy language*

```nix
let
  pkgs = builtins.trace "importing THE UNIVERSE" (import <nixpkgs> {});
in
  1
```

---

### Nix is a *functional* language

::: {.columns}
::: {.column}
A *functional language* is a language whose fundamental unit of composition is the first-class function.

In functional programming, you have to change how you think. Now you're not just passing around objects, you're passing around *functions themselves*!
:::
::: {.column .code-40}
```ts
const nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5];

const sumOfOdds =
  nums
    .filter(n => n % 2 !== 0)
    .reduce((acc, n) => acc + n, 0);

console.log(sumOfOdds); // 9
```

```ts
const nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5];
let sum = 0;

for (const n of nums) {
	if (n % 2 !== 0) {
	  sum += n;
	}
}

return sum;
```
:::
:::

---

### Nix is *pure*

Functions look like this:

```ts
function add(a: number, b: number): number {
  return a + b;
}
```

This would not be possible:

```ts
let total = 0;

function addToTotal(n: number): number {
  total += n;
  return total;
}
```

---

### This is HUGE

When I build something with nix, all its inputs are dependent on all its input, and all those inputs on their inputs, down the nix seed tarball.

```nix
bootstrapTools = import <nix/fetchurl.nix> {
url = "http://tarballs.nixos.org/stdenv-linux/x86_64/c5aabb0d603e2c1ea05f5a93b3be82437f5ebf31/bootstrap-tools.tar.xz";
sha256 = "a5ce9c155ed09397614646c9717fc7cd94b1023d7b76b618d409e4fefd6e9d39";
};
```

---

### And nix has a **crazy**  standard library

You can COMPOSE your builds using totally crazy functions:

```nix
{ pkgs, ... }:
pkgs.buildInLinuxVM {
  name = "super super super duper duper pure and reproducable";
  pkg = pkgs.writeTextFile {
    name = "hello.txt";
    text = "hello world";
    destination = "/hello.txt";
  };
}
```

You can build docker containers with nix, and merge in all your builds:

```nix
{ pkgs, ... }:
pkgs.dockerTools.buildImage {
  name = "gnu-hello";
  tag = "simple";
  contents = [ pkgs.hello ];
  config.Cmd = [ "${pkgs.hello}/bin/hello" ];
}
```

# Some fundamentals

## The "nix store"

![](https://medias.meow.social/media_attachments/files/113/611/636/284/183/702/original/f2acc27aec0593f4.jpg)
 
## The "nix store"

Remember earlier when we said nix functions could return literally anything? Any binary you want!
The nix store is where all of your function results live. Every function result is neatly stuffed into a box, where the name of the box is the hash of the function producing it or the output of the function.

This technique is called a "content addressable store," because, well, everything is addressed by itself, its own *content*.

## The "nix store"

So let's build the hello world from earlier again, but slower:
```
Nix expression
      v eval
Derivation (.drv)
      v realise
Store output
      v consume
Exact file
```

## We hid something from you

How is it reproducible??

We used a `flake.nix`!

```nix
{
  inputs = {
    `nixpkgs.url = "github:nixos/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable";`
  }; # Specify inputs with URIs
  outputs = {self, ...}: {}; # A function!
}
```

## What is a flake?

- An entrypoint
- Like `package.json` or `pyproject.toml` or `Cargo.toml`

Usually, it:

- States which version of the universe (nixpkgs) you want to use for builds and developer environments
- Defines some outputs, like your packages, shells, operating systems, deep dark secrets

## But how does it stay pure? `flake.lock`

## Let's build something else, more nontrivial

I wrote a hello world in `c`!

```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
  printf("Hello, World!\n");
  return 0;
}
```

::: {.code-40}
```nix
{
  description = "C Hello world";

  inputs = {
    flake-utils.url = "github:numtide/flake-utils";
    nixpkgs.url = "github:nixos/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable";
  };

  outputs =
    {
      self,
      nixpkgs,
      flake-utils,
    }:
    flake-utils.lib.eachDefaultSystem ( system:
      let
        pkgs = import nixpkgs { inherit system; };
      in
      {
        packages.default = pkgs.stdenv.mkDerivation {
          pname = "hello";
          version = "1.0";
          src = self; # code at the last commit
          nativeBuildInputs = [ pkgs.gcc ];
          buildPhase = ''
            gcc -o hello ./hello.c
          '';
          installPhase = ''
            mkdir -p $out/bin
            cp hello $out/bin
          '';
        };
      }
    );
}
```
:::
